Zorian is a teenage mage of humble birth and slightly above-average skill, attending his third year of education at Cyoria's magical academy. He is a driven and irritable young man, consumed by a desire to ensure his own future and free himself of the influence of his family, whom he resents for favoring his brothers over him. Consequently, he has no time for pointless distractions or paying attention to other people's problems.

As it happens, time is something he is about to get plenty of. On the eve of the Cyoria's annual summer festival, he is killed and brought back to the beginning of the month, just before he was about to take a train to Cyoria. Suddenly trapped in a time loop with no clear end or exit, Zorian will have to look both within and without to unravel the mystery before him. And he does have to unravel it, for the time loop hadn't been made for his sake and dangers lurk everywhere...

Repetition is the mother of learning, but Zorian will have to first make sure he survives to try again - in a world of magic, even a time traveler isn't safe from those who wish him ill.

This is a collection of what-if scenarios for my other story, Mother of Learning. Time related stories are full of interesting concepts, and alternate timelines are one of them. I've always been fascinated with AU stories, and I've decided to make a few chapters to celebrate getting Mother of Learning official published on Amazon.

(By the way, if you are interested in that, you can find the Amazon link here.)

And yes, this is basically the author making AU fanfiction for his own story. Don't take this too seriously: none of the stories here are canonical and are made purely for fun.

If you aren't familiar with my main story, this will probably not make too much sense to you, but Mother of Learning is a story of a magic-using teenager stuck in a time loop, set in a fantasy world that is in the midst of a technological and magical revolution. If you like what you just read, go hop to the main story and give it a try.

After years of exile, Marcus is coming back home. A powerful mage with few equals, Marcus lives in a world full of monsters and powerful adepts, many of which have bad histories with him. But he has not come back to pursue vengeance or start a fight. All Marcus wants to do is reconnect with old friends, build himself a house, and maybe train a successor or two.

Alas, the world didn’t stop just because Marcus went into exile, and not everyone is content to let go of old grievances. Strange things are happening in the world at large, too, hinting at a looming disaster of unknown nature. Still, where there is a will, there is a way.

If nothing else, Marcus has a lot of magical power to throw at problems.

+++

Zenith of Sorcery is set in its own original setting and isn’t related to Mother of Learning… beyond being written by the same person, of course. This is a more classical fantasy story than my previous one, with a lower level of technology and stuff like elves and dwarves, but it has a lot of worldbuilding effort put into it and its own complex magical system. The story has significant xianxia influences, but isn’t meant to be a xianxia story.

For those of you not familiar with my previous work, I write relatively slowly. I intend to publish chapters at the rate of one chapter every three or four weeks, subject to further delays as life intervenes.

Next Chapter Target Date: September 6th, 2026

The Joker is an interesting addition to a deck of cards. It has next to no use in most games, causing the Joker to be thrown away in most situations. However sometimes the Joker card is kept and is actually cherished by someone. This life of a Joker is the epitome of the life of Coyote Nakamura. He was born an Abnormal Godspawn, a creation of forcing a God to give a human their seed. He was bestowed the power of the Joker. This gives him the power of reversing time whenever he dies and sending his soul back to the desired time. However, it also curses Coyote to get into some of the worst situations possible. This forces Coyote to die hundreds of time until he discovers an answer and survives the situation. Luckily, Coyote has good guidance and decides to become a Dectective. He now uses his powers to stop criminals, terrorists, Demonspawn, and even other Godspawn. 

This is the story of Coyote Nakamura, better known as Detective Joker.

 

*Author's Note*

So, when looking at the basis of the story, this story seems like Mother of Learning. I would say that there is barely anything similar between this and Mother of Learning so be prepared for that. The differences include how the main character will approach the situations, and I would argue this one has a little bit more dramatic in the beginning. It might seem dark at first but don't let that deter you since it won't be dark and heavy forever. Also, the biggest difference is that Mother of Learning is written in a very high level of quality. I wouldn't call my writing bad but it is not compared to the level of that story so don't be too disappointed. Also, the setting for this world is more around early 2000s, but there is magic. I would also like to thank anyone who took the time to read this and comments are always appreciated! Finally, I hope you stick around and enjoy the story!

Walt D. Odell was born in the belt. Like many other Jovean workers, he does 'the long haul'. Moving the most valuable substance in Sol... Water.

It isn't a bad life. Pays well. AI companionship. Excellent healthcare benefits. After 100000 years struggling in the mud the human race got its shit together.

Everything was going great until Walt tries to make a splashdown in the Heinlein Sea. Routine drop and some R&R planned to build up some muscle mass before going back into microgravity.

But the great domed cities of Promethei Terra aren't there.

He can't establish contact with the belt or Earth.

And there's green along the Lowell Canals?

-----

Hello,

I am a professional copywriter who has mainly worked in soul-crushing corporate positions.  Inside sales operations, CRM database administration, and email lead gen... yuck.

And I read terrible, escapest sci-fi.  Sometimes to get through the day.  But, mostly I like it.  Alway have.  Always will.

For a while now I have commented on other stories here on RRL.  I wanted to contribute more.  To share my love for and experience with old school science fiction and fantasy.

Not just Heinlein, Asimov, and Clarke.  But Haggard, Burroughs, Wells, Norton, DeCamp, Howard, Lovecraft, Leiber... all the giants from the golden age. The guys who inspired the modern space program and a million pages of pulp.

I'm currently reading Mother Of Learning (here on RRL) and The Deathworlders (off-site and don't care, HFY all day).

And I suddenly had a question

THIS IS A HUGE SPOILER

Spoiler: Spoiler

What if the entire surface of Mars was an intelligent Von Neumann Machine bent on 'perfecting' all life?

I will be exploring some of my favorite tropes sprinkled with my favorite references once a month as the MC tries to organize himself against the biggest bad I could think of.

Hopefully, I will become a better writer in the process... This is my first effort to write something marketable outside of business academia or the corporate marketing neighborhood.

If it is too technical, verbose, or if the dialogue sucks more donkey dicks than a Tijuana sex show - Please let me know in the comments.

Purpose; a dark fantasy webserial written by Kaysin, starting in late 2023. Updates come every Monday and Thursday, with bonus character chapters for milestones.

Charlotte Haskell's always been a survivor, yet after an unfortunately timed date turns into the apocalypse, she's thrust in a world of fantasy where Dragon's and Demon's aren't just magical, they're true monsters. Left to survive in this new world of Magic, Charlotte has to find her family, protect those around her, stumble through the steps into adulthood, and survive the onslaught from another world, all while learning about her new powers, and combating the demonic forces that threaten to destroy mankind.

Purpose; isn't for the faint of heart, and touches on dark theme's and death more than your average serial. Characters die, people are various shades of greyed out morality, and the world is brutal and unrelenting. The main character does not always make the right decision, and sometimes makes disagreeable ones, and while is the focus point we follow, isn't a chosen one, or the center of the world by any means at the start of her journey. If you can't handle acts of extreme violence, suffering, depressing overtones, and constant dire circumstances, then Purpose; may not be for you. That said, I do my best not to veer off into torture porn - the world is unrelenting, but there's hope, and that's one of the few things that guide the characters.

I started writing Purpose; as a need for well, Purpose, hence the name, inspired by Dazai Osamu's "No Longer Human", in which the character's goal in life is stated to be "Nothing". I don't work full time, and spend most of my year indoors, watching after my mother who can no longer work. My hopes is to one day make it as an author of some renown, and support her by giving her, and the people around me, the life they deserve to lead. Donations, by proxy, are greatly appreciated, as I want to give her the world before she gets too old to see it. I wear my inspirations on my sleeves, and she's one of them; but also the authors that have genuinely changed my life. Wildbow, known for his holy trinity of Worm, Pact and Twig, along with authors such a Hazel Young known for their series Katalepsis, the more recent Anemone and their wonderful stories Nowhere Stars, and of course the goat, Domagoi Krurmaic and his amazing work, Mother of Learning. Each have influenced me in some tiny way, and if you see similarities between the stories, know that they're inspired from a place of profound respect and admiration.

I typically write at a pace of 5k words a day on good days, or 2-3k on bad days, and I maintain a small backlog, especially well into the first and second arcs. I intend to write Purpose; for a long time coming, so please bare with me on this ride as I grow as an author.

Sable Voss Lucthilde grew up in the Dredge. That means flooded tunnels, poisoned air, and a Rain that kills thirty-five thousand people every cycle while the people above count the bodies and call it policy.

When the Rain finally gives him a Grace, it’s this: genuine regret rewinds time by sixty seconds.

Not fire. Not strength. Just enough rope to hang himself with twice.

But Sable is patient. And he’s been writing down the names of everyone who deserves to die for a very long time.

The bird on his shoulder used to be a robin. It’s something else now. The boy beside him blows things up with his feet and refuses to leave. The girl he carried out of the Dredge is eight years old and learning what it means to refuse to be eaten.

And somewhere above all of them, five Houses are voting on whether people like Sable get to exist.

They should have killed him when they had the chance.

 CONTENT WARNING

Graphic violence and death Morally gray/dark protagonist Child endangerment situations Psychological trauma and mental degradation Dark themes including murder, survival, and moral ambiguity Time loop mechanics with permanent consequences
